req.title: Redirect count boundary
req.statement: The system shall accept /redirect/<n> with n in the range 1..30 inclusive and reject values above.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states /redirect/<n> must accept n in [1..30] inclusive and reject values above 30. Key boundaries are: n=1 (lower bound), n=30 (upper bound), n=31 (first invalid above upper bound), n=0 (below lower bound via assert). The source code shows `assert n > 0` (which raises AssertionError for n=0, yielding 500) and the route uses `<int:n>` so non-integers yield 404. For n>30, httpbin does not explicitly cap at 30 in the shown source — however the requirement states rejection above 30. We test the full boundary set: n=1 (BVA lower), n=15 (EP mid-range), n=30 (BVA upper), n=31 (NEG above upper), n=0 (NEG below lower). We follow redirects manually by checking the initial 302 status and Location header, since the test client by default does not follow redirects. For n=1 the redirect goes directly to /get (200 after following). We assert exact status codes to catch comparison-operator mutations.

tests.name: test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_accepted
preconditions: n=1 is the minimum valid redirect count
trace: R-HTTPBIN-048: n=1 is lower boundary of valid range [1..30]
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_accepted():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert '/get' in location or location.endswith('/get')
    r2 = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r2.status_code == 200

test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_accepted()

actions: Assert response is NOT 2xx (must be 4xx or 5xx)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-048: values above 30 must be rejected; n=31 is first invalid value above upper bound
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n31_above_upper_boundary_rejected():
    r = client.get('/redirect/31', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code >= 400, f'Expected 4xx/5xx for n=31, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 302

tests.name: test_redirect_n1_follows_to_get_endpoint
expected: Response body is JSON with 'url' key (from /get handler)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-048: n=1 is valid; source code shows `if n == 1: return redirect(url_for('view_get'))`
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n1_follows_to_get_endpoint():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = json.loads(r.data)
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'headers' in data

test_redirect_n1_follows_to_get_endpoint()

expected: Status code == 404 because Flask cannot convert 'abc' to int
trace: R-HTTPBIN-048: error pathway for non-integer n; Flask int converter rejects non-numeric strings

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_non_integer_path_rejected():
    r = client.get('/redirect/abc', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 404

test_redirect_non_integer_path_rejected()

tests.name: test_redirect_n30_not_same_as_n31
preconditions: n=30 accepted, n=31 rejected — both sides of boundary tested together
trace: R-HTTPBIN-048: BVA catches comparison-operator mutation (> vs >= on limit 30)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n30_not_same_as_n31():
    r30 = client.get('/redirect/30', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r30.status_code == 302
    r31 = client.get('/redirect/31', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r31.status_code != 302
    assert r31.status_code != 200
    assert r31.status_code >= 400

test_redirect_n30_not_same_as_n31()
